description: Stash additions (accepted and rejected) and Core placement rules.
Placing from the stash: each placement rejection, then accepted placements.
Moving, rotating, returning and removing buildings.
Owners in a two-player party.

PP-1: only the owner places, moves, returns or removes a building (not_owner); a footprint or conduit cell in a neighbour's plot is outside_own_plot; a conduit crossing the border is rejected; only the owner erases a conduit.
Every conduit rejection reason, direct and path conduits, erase, and detaching on move and return.
A splitter, a merger and a crossover carrying two resources, all conduits accepted.
A merger mismatch that only appears when the upstream source is connected last, and a loop through two splitters and a merger.
One Core per player: outside_own_plot, a second player's Core, core_already_placed per player, overlaps_core with any Core.
Halves at a border spot: each new refusal, a join, a mismatch that only appears across the link, an erase that leaves an open half and the rejoin refused.
A loop closed through two links is refused; direct halves (no cells) join as a link of length 0.

A conduit leaving a refinery carries its output resource (CB-5b): Composite from the Composite refinery is refused with resource_mismatch at the Aether refinery's input (either one) and at a Barracks (Ore). A Flux collector then feeds the same Aether refinery's west input without trouble.

Rich vein (RS-4i4): nodes added to a plot (accepted and each rejection: a node or feature or Core or building already there, the front row, another plot, an unknown resource or round, the cap of 3 per plot), then an extractor built on an added node and a wall refused on one (node_reserved). The state carries addedNodes in the order added.

Tunnel pairing (CB-9g): an entrance pairs with the exit in the direction it faces, with at most 5 cells between (distance 6): pairs at distance 4 (north) and 6 (the longest); an exit 6 cells away (distance 7) is out of range, so both ends stay unpaired; an entrance turned east pairs with an exit in its row, and a nearer exit placed later takes the pair over (nearest wins); an end of owner 1 in owner 0's plot is refused with outside_own_plot; owner 1's own pair is separate. Each result lists the pairs [entrance, exit, distance] after the op.

Tunnel pairing, nearest wins (CB-9g): one entrance and two exits in its line take the nearer exit whatever the placing order; two entrances facing the same exit give it to the nearer one, and the other stays unpaired (it does not fall back to the farther exit behind); two entrances at the same distance from one exit from opposite sides give it to the lower building ID.

Tunnel pairing follows the placement (CB-9g): moving the exit out of line unpairs, moving it nearer re-pairs at the shorter distance, a farther exit does not change a pair, turning the entrance away unpairs and back re-pairs, picking up the nearer exit brings the farther one into the pair, moving the entrance changes the distance, a move onto the entrance is refused (overlaps_building), and picking up the entrance unpairs everything.

A Tunnel pair is a conduit segment, so it counts for loops (CB-9c): the entrance (fed by a Merger) pairs with the nearer exit; the farther exit feeds a Splitter whose east output runs back to the Merger. That ring is accepted while the nearer exit stands (the farther exit is unpaired). Picking up the nearer exit, or moving it out of line, would pair the entrance with the farther exit and close the loop, so both are refused with would_loop (and nothing changes); turning the farther exit instead detaches its conduit first and is accepted.

A Tunnel pair carries one resource fixed by its input conduit (CB-5b): Ore enters the entrance, the exit it pairs with has no conduit, and the farther exit feeds a Hangar (Power). Picking up or moving the nearer exit, which would carry Ore to the Hangar, is refused with resource_mismatch.

Specialists (issue #470, RS-13): a pick sets one player's entry and leaves the others null; a pick can be changed; duplicates are allowed; an ID outside the roster and a player outside the party are refused and change nothing. The state has no `specialists` field before the first pick (so it hashes as before) and the field afterwards. Clearing the only pick with null drops the field again.
Setting a player's specialist to null removes the entry; with no entry left the `specialists` field is omitted again, as in a state from before specialists.

Mana Well and the building resource setting (issue #473): a Well stands on any open cell of its owner's plot, with no node needed (without a resource it takes the first base resource), also on a node (whose resource it ignores); a natural feature, another player's plot, a resource that is not a base resource and a resource given to a building without the setting are refused. The setting is stored on the placed building only. Changing it to a different resource detaches the attached conduit (the same resource changes nothing); a Flux Well cannot be wired to an Ore input; a move keeps the setting; returning to the stash drops it.
